summary.goal: HEAVY SUMO block, squat moderate (alternating-axial-emphasis; B6 was the reverse). Sumo walks 345 -> 365 -> 385 -> 405 inside sumo-back-cap (@7 hard cap, reps <=4, 405 is the hard ceiling), and EVERY rung is gated on the Saturday morning back check: fine = next rung, tight or no check = repeat the load, two 'sore' in a row = axial work stops. The squat drops to a flat fixed 365 -> 395 @7 so only one axial lift is heavy at a time. Bench gets the first real change to its stimulus in four blocks: a SECOND comp-bench exposure at six reps on D4, in the slot CGB vacated. Dip peaks W3, bench peaks W4 — never the same week. Pull-up is capped by absolute load for the elbows. W5 deloads.
changes: AXIAL EMPHASIS FLIPS: sumo heavy, squat moderate. B6 ran squat heavy / sumo moderate.

SUMO 345 / 365 / 385 / 405 (deload 295), triples with 3-3-3-2-3 backoff sets at ~88%. @7 is a HARD cap, not a target. 405 is the hard ceiling of sumo-back-cap and it is the ceiling because the clinic is SIX BLOCKS OWED — not because it is your limit. Each rung gated on the back check; B6 gave 1 check in 10 axial sessions and sumo then self-advanced +30 lb over a written fixed band, so the gate is a table this block, not prose.

SQUAT moderate: flat 365 / 375 / 385 / 395 x3 x3 @7 (deload 315), fixed, NO range and no autoregulating up. It will feel light three weeks after 435x3 @7.5 — that is the trade. A 415 Monday squat plus a 405 Friday pull is two heavy axial days a week on a treated back with no clinical clearance.

COMP BENCH TWICE A WEEK. D1 heavy: 255x3 -> 265x3 -> 270x2 -> 280x2, 'work up to @8' with a floor and a lid (255/265 -> 265/275 -> 270/285 -> 280/295), backoffs 4-4-4-3-3 at x4 reps. D4 volume: 210 / 215 / 220 / 225 x6, FIXED at @7, four sets (three in W4). Sixes because 'loses arch under fatigue' is the bench weak point and a double never exposes it. Bench-pattern volume is near-neutral vs B6 (12 -> 13 sets) — it is redistributed onto the competition lift. B6 logged the identical set at the identical RPE as B5 (275x2 @8.5); the input had to change, not the number.
D1 ORDER CHANGED: bench goes FIRST, ahead of the moderate squat. First block where the priority lift gets the fresh body. D4: sumo first, always.

PULL-UP capped by ABSOLUTE LOAD, not RPE: BW+55 / 65 / 75 / 85 x3-4 fixed, 3 backoffs. Tops at BW+85, under B6's +95 and B5's +90. Two independent reasons — BOTH elbows (pain on flexion; left since ~late September) and heavy sumo on D4. GRIP: wider than shoulder, PRONATED, explicitly NOT neutral (your 10-22 note: 'right inner elbow pain with the nuetral grip'). cap-is-a-target is SUSPENDED for this lift: a hard stop held for two blocks, a range broke it in one (@9.5 in B6 W4).
DIP unchanged because it works: W3 peak (work up to @8, floor BW+105x3, lid BW+115), then HOLDS at BW+95 in W4 so it never peaks the same week as the bench. Depth before load.

SECONDARIES — 1 rotation. Spoto HELD on D3 (250/255/255/265 x3 x3 @7.5): it has progressed every session for two blocks. CGB OUT after three blocks; its slot became the second comp-bench exposure. Squat and deadlift secondary pools are still fully Blocked - medical, so the heavy-sumo block has no barbell lockout secondary — Hip Thrust (D2) carries that.

SUPERSETS REMOVED from W2-D3 on (FB 2026-11-11, superset-same-equipment): all six B7 pairs put a machine on at least one side, and you can't hold one machine while working another. Every accessory now runs straight sets. Named first cuts if the tail bleeds: D1 Iso-Lateral Row, D2 Lateral Raise, D3 Face Pull, D4 Seated Calf Raise.
W1 IS A WORKING WEEK, not a calibration week (FB 2026-10-12: no warm-up week after a deload). Primaries push at the full 1:15 rest from day one; only W5 drops to 1:00.
accessory_changes: NEW: Straight Arm Lat Pulldown (D2), 45 -> 50 x12. Straight arms mean ZERO elbow-flexion load, so it is the lat stimulus the elbows currently forbid everywhere else — exactly while the pull-up is being held back. Also loads serratus, which drives scapular upward rotation and the subacromial space the bursitis sits in. 28 sessions in the log but all 2022-2023, so the 61 lb median is history: it opens at 45 and is pinned until the log re-establishes the level (secondary-first-exposure).

BACK IN: Hip Adduction (Machine) (D4), 105 -> 115 x15. Sumo-stance-specific adductors in the heavy-sumo block. 90 sessions, last trained 09-20 at 105, so the anchor is your real 105-115, not the 90s. After sumo, never before.

OUT: Concentration Curl. Direct elbow flexion, and both elbows hurt on flexion — your own 'doesnt use the bicep' note is the argument for it. Biceps get their dose from the wide-grip pull and the two row slots. Back when the elbows are quiet.

OUT: Bulgarian Split Squat. A heavy-sumo block cannot carry loaded unilateral leg work in the 48 h either side of a 405 pull, and every day already has its lower dose without it (squat D1, hip thrust + leg curl D2, leg extension D3, sumo D4). Out for a reason, not for time. This takes D4 from 7 exercises to 6 and it brushes your 'don't reduce the count' rule — flagged rather than slipped past. Say the word and it comes back on D2.

PINNED LOWER TO PROTECT FRIDAY: Lat Pulldown held at 145-150 against a 157 median, because D3 is the day before a 345-405 sumo and the lats hold the bar. Leg Extension flat at 135. Iso-Lateral Row still pinned at 120-125 to protect Tuesday's pull-up.

SHOULDER SLOTS unchanged and still at a hard @7: Single Arm Landmine Press (diagonal path, least subacromial compression available) and Reverse Pec Deck (the intact posterior cuff sharing load off two torn anterior tendons). Barbell OHP, upright row and barbell incline stay blocked in the movement library.

CORE: four patterns, one per day, unchanged — Side Plank (anti-lateral-flexion), Pallof (anti-rotation), Dead Bug (anti-extension), Bird Dog (spine-neutral). No loaded lumbar flexion, no hanging leg raise while the back is under treatment.
DELIBERATE COVERAGE GAPS, both named with reasons: no direct erector loading (back under treatment) and no direct biceps work (the elbows). Everything else covered.

Work up to @8 and STOP: floor 270, lid 285 - take the heaviest set at or under @8. Going above the floor is not creep; going above the lid is. Backoffs 4x4 @ 225. Shoulder: <=3/10 pain on every rep, always. Arch and upper back stay set - losing the arch under fatigue is the weak point this block is built around.

exercises.name: Low-bar Squat
exercises.hold_reason: Squat is the MODERATE axial lift this block (alternating-axial-emphasis): a fixed band that tops at 395, well under B6's 435 peak, so the axial budget goes to heavy sumo. Written below the log on purpose; the sync must not rebase it.
exercises.notes: W3 PUSH - MODERATE, FIXED. 385x3 x3, @7 ceiling. This is not a floor and there is no range: do not autoregulate upward. B6's sumo was written exactly this way and climbed +30 lb on feel - that is the mistake this wording exists to stop. You squatted 435x3 @7.5 three weeks ago, so 385 will feel easy. That is the point: sumo is taking the axial load this block and the squat is holding its groove.

exercises.name: Tricep Pushdown
exercises.notes: Lockout (bench weak point) -> triceps. Stop at @8. Alt: Cable Triceps Extension, same load.

exercises.name: Chest Fly (Machine)
exercises.notes: Pec isolation without a fifth press. STOP the handles before the elbows travel behind the torso - the stretched bottom loads the anterior capsule where the subscapularis tear sits. Alt: Seated Cable Fly 70.

exercises.name: Iso-Lateral Row (Machine)
exercises.notes: Per arm, one at a time. Monday's pull dose (whole-body-every-day), chest-supported, zero lumbar load. Held under the 135 median so it does not pre-fatigue Tuesday's pull-up. FIRST CUT on D1 if the morning runs out or Tuesday's backoffs suffer. Alt: CS Incline Row (DB) 45/hand. Never T-bar or bent-over.
exercises.hold_reason: Deliberately under the 135 log median: D1 row must not pre-fatigue D2 weighted pull-up, which is already elbow-limited this block.

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.notes: Anti-lateral-flexion. 30-45 s per side.

exercises.name: Weighted Pull-up
exercises.hold_reason: Capped by ABSOLUTE load for two independent reasons: BOTH elbows (anterior, pain on flexion; left since ~late Sept 2026, right from late Oct) and heavy sumo on D4 (CLAUDE.md - pull-up volume drops when deadlift volume is high). Tops at BW+85, under B6's BW+95 and B5's BW+90, on purpose. The sync must not rebase it.
exercises.notes: W3 PUSH - FIXED LOAD BW+75x3, no range, no 'work up to'. Backoffs BW+45x5 x3. ELBOWS (both, anterior - left since ~late Sept, right from late Oct): GRIP WIDER THAN SHOULDER WIDTH, PRONATED. NOT neutral - your own 10-22 note says the neutral grip is what hurt the right inner elbow. Wide felt slightly weaker to you and that is the right trade. Any pain DURING a set ends the exercise for the day - don't finish the set. Report it the same day. Fixed load, not an RPE target: a sore tendon can't be autoregulated. Why it is lower than B6: the elbow is live AND this is the heavy-sumo block, so the back/lat/grip budget goes to Friday. Chin over the bar every rep or the set is over.

exercises.name: Straight Arm Lat Pulldown (Cable)
exercises.notes: NEW THIS BLOCK (last trained Nov 2023). Straight arms - ZERO elbow flexion, which is the whole point: it is the lat stimulus the elbow currently forbids everywhere else. Also loads serratus, which helps scapular upward rotation and the subacromial space. Soft elbows, move at the shoulder only. Opens well under the stale 61 lb anchor. Alt: Rope Straight Arm Pulldown.
exercises.hold_reason: 3-year-gap re-entry: 28 sessions but all 2022-2023, median 61 lb. Per secondary-first-exposure a stale anchor is history, not a starting point - open under it and let the log re-establish the level.

exercises.name: Hip Thrust (Smith Machine)
exercises.notes: Sumo lockout / out of the hole -> glutes. This is the hitch work: the deadlift secondary pool is entirely blocked medical, so the glutes get trained here instead. Tuesday, three days clear of Friday's pull. Alt: Glute Bridge (Barbell) 185.

exercises.name: Seated Leg Curl
exercises.notes: Hamstrings, knee-flexion side. Alt: Lying Leg Curl.

exercises.name: Lateral Raise (Dumbbell)
exercises.notes: Lateral delts. FIRST CUT on D2 if the morning runs out. Alt: Cable Lateral Raise 20.

exercises.name: Single Arm Landmine Press (Barbell)
exercises.notes: Per arm. Front delts on a diagonal path - less subacromial compression than any overhead press. @7 CAP, and that cap is the shoulder's, not a preference: two low-grade partial tears plus bursitis. Load is plates on the sleeve, not counting the bar. Alt: Neutral-grip DB Press (seated) 45, same @7 cap. NEVER barbell OHP.
exercises.hold_reason: Shoulder slot under a hard @7 cap (two partial-thickness tears + subacromial bursitis). The cap, not the log, sets this load.

exercises.name: Pallof Press
exercises.notes: Anti-rotation. Slow, no hip rotation.

exercises.name: Weighted Dip
exercises.notes: W3 PUSH - DIP PEAK. Work up to @8: floor BW+105x3, lid BW+115. Take the heaviest triple at or under @8. Your best is BW+105x3 @7.5 and you did BW+95x5 @6 the same morning, so there is real reserve here - this is the one lift where the cap is a target. DEPTH BEFORE LOAD: stop above the pinch, every rep.

exercises.name: Spoto Bench Press
exercises.notes: W3 PUSH - 255x3 x3, @7.5 ceiling. HELD, not rotated: it has progressed every single session for two blocks and it is the only bench movement with an unbroken upward record. Pause an inch off the chest, dead stop, then drive - it trains the sticking point. Holds at 255 this week because the dip peaks today.

exercises.name: Lat Pulldown
exercises.notes: Lats, seated, no axial load. HELD WELL UNDER the 157 median this block - tomorrow is a 345-405 sumo and the lats hold the bar. Alt: Natural Grip Pulldown, same load. ELBOW: wide pronated grip here too - the 10-22 'right inner elbow pain with the neutral grip' note was on THIS exercise. No neutral bar.
exercises.hold_reason: Held under the 157 log median on purpose: D3 lat work must not pre-fatigue D4, which is HEAVY sumo this block. This is a sumo-protection pin, not a progression target.

exercises.name: Leg Extension (Machine)
exercises.notes: Thursday's lower-body dose (whole-body-every-day) and the lowest-cost option that exists before a heavy Friday pull: no spinal load, no loaded hip flexion, no adductor cost. Alt: Leg Press 270, ROM-capped. NO squat pattern, NO hinge, NO adductor work on D3 this block.
exercises.hold_reason: Flat at/under the 135-140 median: D3 quad work must not pre-fatigue D4 heavy sumo.

exercises.name: Reverse Pec Deck
exercises.notes: @7 CAP - shoulder slot. Load-bearing work: the intact posterior cuff shares load off two torn anterior tendons. Alt: Rear Delt Fly (DB) 25.
exercises.hold_reason: Shoulder slot under a hard @7 cap. Ran to @9.5 in B5 under this same cap; the cap sets the load, not the log.

exercises.name: Face Pull
exercises.notes: External rotation + scapular control. @7. FIRST CUT on D3 if the morning runs out (same target family as the pec deck). Alt: Band pull-apart x20.

exercises.name: Dead Bug
exercises.notes: Anti-extension. Ribs down, low back flat to the floor.

exercises.name: Sumo Deadlift
exercises.hold_reason: HEAVY sumo under sumo-back-cap (band 345-405, @7 cap, reps <=4, 405 hard ceiling) AND still on axial-return-ladder: every rung is an absolute load gated on the next-morning back check. Never rebase this from the log.
exercises.notes: W3 PUSH - SUMO IS THE BLOCK. Floor 385x3 -> lid 395, backoffs 345x3 x3. sumo-back-cap: @7 is a HARD cap, reps <=4, every rep crisp, 405 is the hard ceiling. Any back rounding or bar-speed drop -> rack it. NEVER grind sumo. RANGE (added 2026-11-08, athlete: 'push a little more'): floor 385, lid 395. Only if the floor triple is <=@7 AND the warm-ups move fast, take one more triple at 395 - heaviest set at or under @7 counts. Going above the floor inside the range is not creep; going above the lid is. Backoffs stay at 345 off the FLOOR. Next week's floor does NOT move with what the range reached. GATE: this rung is unlocked only by Saturday's back check on last week's pull reading `fine`. `tight` -> repeat last week's load. No check logged -> repeat last week's load. Two `sore` in a row -> axial work stops, back to the clinic. Sumo goes FIRST on D4, always. Tall lockout, no hitch - if it hitches above the knee the weight is too heavy for today regardless of what the plan says.

exercises.name: Comp Bench
exercises.notes: W3 PUSH - SECOND COMP-BENCH EXPOSURE, and the whole reason this block exists for your bench. 220x6 x4, FIXED, @7 ceiling. This is not a second heavy day - do not chase it. Sixes, because 'loses arch under fatigue' is your bench weak point and a double never exposes it. Hold the arch and the upper back on rep 6 exactly as on rep 1; if the arch collapses, the set is over even if the reps are there. Shoulder <=3/10. Bench goes AFTER sumo today.

exercises.name: Seated Calf Raise
exercises.notes: Calves. FIRST CUT on D4 if the morning runs out. NO standing or barbell calf raise as a fallback - axial compression, and the back is under treatment.

exercises.name: Chest Supported Incline Row
exercises.notes: Mid-back, chest-supported, zero lumbar load - which is why it is the row that survives on a heavy-pull day. Alt: Seated Cable Row 120. NEVER barbell bent-over.

exercises.name: Sumo Deadlift
exercises.hold_reason: HEAVY sumo under sumo-back-cap (band 345-405, @7 cap, reps <=4, 405 hard ceiling) AND still on axial-return-ladder: every rung is an absolute load gated on the next-morning back check. Never rebase this from the log.
exercises.notes: W5 DELOAD - SUMO IS THE BLOCK. 295x3, backoffs 265x3 x3. sumo-back-cap: @7 is a HARD cap, reps <=4, every rep crisp, 405 is the hard ceiling. Any back rounding or bar-speed drop -> rack it. NEVER grind sumo. GATE: this rung is unlocked only by Saturday's back check on last week's pull reading `fine`. `tight` -> repeat last week's load. No check logged -> repeat last week's load. Two `sore` in a row -> axial work stops, back to the clinic. Sumo goes FIRST on D4, always. Tall lockout, no hitch - if it hitches above the knee the weight is too heavy for today regardless of what the plan says.

exercises.name: Comp Bench
exercises.notes: W5 DELOAD - SECOND COMP-BENCH EXPOSURE, and the whole reason this block exists for your bench. 185x6 x3, FIXED, @7 ceiling. This is not a second heavy day - do not chase it. Sixes, because 'loses arch under fatigue' is your bench weak point and a double never exposes it. Hold the arch and the upper back on rep 6 exactly as on rep 1; if the arch collapses, the set is over even if the reps are there. Shoulder <=3/10. Bench goes AFTER sumo today.
